A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSD research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated content and genuinely removed visual examples.

before.justification: v4 reports original RSD training and evaluation results, quantitative ablations, computational measurements, and higher-resolution training experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results, including real-world and synthetic super-resolution evaluations, loss and update-frequency ablations, and the higher-resolution experiment.

M1.justification: The architecture, fake-model distillation, multistep training, LPIPS/GAN components, and single-step inference are retained. Algorithm 1's revised timestep sampling matches the subset already specified in v4 Section 3.3; the sampling references and explicit discriminator maximization clarify existing procedures rather than establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both retain ImageNet and LSDIR training and evaluation on RealSR, RealSet65, DRealSR, RealLR200, RealLQ250, ImageNet-Test, and DIV2K. Added baseline results and removed visual examples do not change the represented datasets, tasks, or degradation scenarios.

E2.justification: v5 adds FluxSR to the full-size DRealSR, RealLR200, RealLQ250, and RealSR/RealSet65 comparisons in Tables 13–15. It adds D3SR to RealSR/RealSet65 in Table 15 and DIV2K-Val in Table 17. The existing quantitative comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Table 4 revises the reported TSD-SR training hardware from eight A100 GPUs to eight V100 GPUs, retaining 96 hours. This changes the stated resource basis of the training-time comparison without establishing a rerun. RSD's training budgets, crop sizes, evaluation metrics, and testing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 removes the visual analysis of LPIPS/GAN effects in v4 Figure 9 and the synthetic DIV2K failure cases in v4 Figure 13, and reduces other failure examples. The quantitative loss, timestep, and update-frequency ablations, convergence analysis, and higher-resolution training experiment remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and the same training-convergence curves. Neither provides repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons.

E6.justification: Besides the added FluxSR and D3SR result rows, Table 15 changes CTMSR's RealSR MUSIQ from 64.782 to 64.796 and RealSet65 CLIPIQA/MUSIQ from 0.6871/67.032 to 0.6893/67.173, matching Table 1. RSD's matched numerical results remain unchanged, while several qualitative output comparisons are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix L adds an exact distribution-matching proof under explicit ideal teacher/fake recovery assumptions, Equations 47–54. Appendix A.1 corrects the noise multiplier from kappa-squared times eta_t to kappa times sqrt(eta_t), and replaces an incorrect conditional–marginal equality with averaging over generator outputs. These substantively revise the objective's mathematical justification; Proposition 3.1 itself is retained.

C1.justification: The main novelty, single-step restoration, perceptual-performance, and efficiency contributions remain. The introduction replaces the blanket tenfold parameter disadvantage for T2I methods with a 2.5–10-fold statement, accommodating smaller comparators such as AdcSR, listed at 456M parameters versus 174M for SinSR/RSD in Table 4.

C2.justification: Appendix L newly explains the ideal recovery conditions behind its distribution-matching argument. v5 removes the detailed interpretation of supervised losses' texture/blur effects and the discussion of synthetic DIV2K failures. The broader teacher-capacity and perception–distortion limitations remain.

D1.justification: v5 adds an explicit RSD code link, identifies sources for FluxSR outputs and borrowed D3SR scores, and aligns Algorithm 1 with the documented timestep subset. It also revises TSD-SR hardware information and removes some detailed Table 17 baseline-result provenance. Most implementation settings and checkpoint information are retained.

R1.justification: FluxSR and D3SR introduce two additional cited works and empirical positioning against newer SR methods. The substantive relationships to VSD, SiD, FGM, IBMD, and AddSR remain largely unchanged. PiSA-SR publication metadata updates and removal of a duplicate CLIPIQA reference do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: v5 makes widespread local grammar edits, updates affiliations and publication information, adds acknowledgements, and condenses baseline descriptions. The LLM disclosure moves from Appendix M to D, and additional ablations move after the higher-resolution study. The main narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v5 removes v4 Figures 9, 13, and 14–17, shortens the image grids corresponding to v4 Figures 5, 6, and 10–12, and substantially redistributes retained figures and tables. Tables gain baseline rows, while retained image panels are unchanged. This substantially changes the visual presentation and available illustrative evidence.

improvement.justification: The mathematical corrections, explicit recovery assumptions, consistent CTMSR reporting, and code access instructions provide a modest net improvement in reliability and assessability. These gains are partly offset by removal of the visual loss ablation and several failure examples; Appendix K also retains a reference to the deleted road-and-cars panel. The new proof addresses ideal exact matching rather than approximate errors, and RSD's numerical evidence is unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
